name: Aruba

support.name: DEACI: Department of Economic Affairs, Commerce and Industry

legalStatuses.label: Sole trader (registered business)
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.feeNote: The Chamber of Commerce quotes the registration fee. You also need a business licence for your activity.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company (an NV or a VBA, the two company forms) costs more to set up than a sole proprietorship. The Chamber of Commerce quotes the current fees.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
launchSteps.plain: Search the name at the Chamber of Commerce first.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Chamber of Commerce
launchSteps.plain: Every business registers in the commercial register. A company is incorporated through a notary.

launchSteps.label: Apply for your business licence
launchSteps.plain: Most activities need a licence. DEACI explains the steps and the documents.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Tax Department
launchSteps.plain: You get your tax number and your turnover tax (BBO) account. File your returns even in months without sales.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Social Insurance Bank (SVb)
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people pay old age and widow/orphan insurance (AOV and AWW, the two pension insurances) on their own income.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register your employees and prepare payroll payments
launchSteps.plain: With employees you pay wage tax, AOV/AWW and AZV health insurance each month.

incomeTax.label: Income tax
incomeTax.bracketText: 0% on the first Afl. 34,930 after the tax-free amount, 21% up to Afl. 63,904, 42% up to Afl. 135,527, then 52%

salesLevies.label: Turnover tax (BBO, plus BAZV and BAVP, two earmarked levies collected with it)

contributions.label: Old age and widow/orphan insurance (AOV/AWW)
contributions.plain: A pension insurance. Self-employed people pay 13.5% of their income, up to Afl. 85,000 a year. The Social Insurance Bank also tells you which health insurance premium applies to you.

calendar.monthlyText: File and pay your turnover tax (BBO) for the previous period. The Tax Department gives you the filing dates when you register.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay wage tax, AOV/AWW and AZV for the previous month.

notes: Aruba has no VAT. Businesses pay a turnover tax (BBO, BAZV and BAVP together: 7%) on their sales. The first Afl. 50,000 of yearly sales is exempt for small entrepreneurs.
Your yearly income tax is calculated after the Afl. 30,000 tax-free amount.

The government is studying a switch from the turnover tax to a VAT (talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in March 2026). Nothing is decided: your estimate uses the current 7% turnover tax.
